name: python-polylith-cb0ac4b0-blind28-ots
instr:
# Diagnosing broken workspace behaviour in python-polylith without a test suite

This checkout holds the tooling a team uses to keep one repository full of small reusable units and the several deliverable projects assembled out of them: it reads the declaration files, works out who uses what, and gets each deliverable ready to install. A great many everyday operations now answer wrongly or fail on inputs that used to be routine. The repository has received 28 separate undocumented edits. Nothing about the declaration formats changed and nothing about the way they are called changed; the same questions that used to be answered correctly are now answered wrongly, and in several places a question that used to be answered at all now errors.

Finding out which outside libraries a deliverable asks for, by reading its declaration file, goes wrong in two ways at once. A requirement written in the older table-and-marker style \u2014 a version held in a table, or an entry qualified by an interpreter marker \u2014 comes back with an empty version string, while a requirement given as a plain string still reads back exactly as declared. Listing only the names behind those requirements is worse: a requirement carrying extras in square brackets yields scrambled text rather than the package name together with each of its extras, which makes the listing useless.
